label: Four definitions of economics
text: Adam Smith (1776): the nature and causes of the wealth of nations. Alfred Marshall (1890): a study of man in the ordinary business of life and the material requisites of well-being. Lionel Robbins (1932): human behaviour as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses. Paul Samuelson (1948): how societies use scarce resources to produce valuable commodities and distribute them among different people.

label: Managerial economics questions
text: What price should a firm charge for its product? How much output should be produced? How many workers should be hired?

label: Accounting cost and opportunity cost examples
text: Accounting costs: wages, rent, electricity, raw materials. Opportunity cost: owner's time, foregone salary, own building used for business.

label: Factors that affect profitability
text: A star labelled Sustainable Industry Profits with five boxes pointing at it: Entry, Power of Input Suppliers, Power of Buyers, Industry Rivalry, and Substitutes & Complements.

label: Sales representative incentive
text: Firm's goal: increase sales. Employee's incentive: earn a sales commission. Result: higher effort, higher sales, higher earnings for the employee and higher profits for the firm.

label: ₹10,000 today or in a year
text: Would you prefer ₹10,000 today or ₹10,000 one year from now? The opportunity cost of waiting a year is the interest foregone that could be earned from investing ₹10,000 today.

label: Advertising intensity case
text: Three advertising intensities for a new model, discounted at 10%: High $303.31M, Low $256.76M, Moderate $214.39M. High maximizes the present value even though it has the lowest profits in Years 1-2.

label: $5,000 machine
text: Cost $5000, $2000 a year for 3 years at 7%: PV = $5,248.63, NPV = 5,248.63 - 5000 = $248.63. NPV > 0, so the firm should buy the machine.

label: Break-room refrigerator
text: Energy-efficient model at $550 saving $28 at the end of each of the next 5 years, or a standard model at $420 with no savings; opportunity cost of funds 5 percent. Which should you buy?

label: Deferred perpetuity endowment
text: An endowment pays $800 per year forever, with the first payment at the end of Year 5, at an interest rate of 6%. What is its present value today?

label: Firm with constant $50,000 profits
text: Profits of $50,000 paid out as dividends forever, first paid at the end of this year, i = 10%: PV(firm) = 0 + 50,000 / 0.10 = $500,000.

label: Software company valuation scenarios
text: Current profits $3.2 billion (not yet paid), interest rate 9 percent; value the firm if profits grow at 11%, 4%, 0%, or decline at 4% a year.

label: Thinking at the margin questions
text: Should the firm produce one more unit of a product? Should it hire one more worker? Should it spend ₹10,000 more on advertising? Answer: only if the additional benefit exceeds the additional cost.

label: Discrete and continuous decision examples
text: Discrete: hire one more worker, open another store. Continuous: set the selling price, decide advertising expenditure.

label: MR and MC table (outputs 0 to 6)
text: TR rises by 50 per unit (0 to 300) while TC goes 20, 40, 70, 110, 160, 220, 290. MC rises 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70, so MR = MC = 50 at output 4.

label: Whole-units practice schedule
text: Q from 0 to 6 with TR 0, 90, 170, 240, 300, 350, 390 and TC 0, 50, 90, 140, 200, 270, 350. Which quantity maximizes profit?

label: TR = 50Q - Q², TC = 10Q
text: Profit 50Q - Q² - 10Q; MR = MC gives Q = 20; second order condition -2 < 0; profit = 50 * 20 - 20 * 20 - 10 * 20 = $400.

label: Monopolist practice question
text: A monopolist faces demand P = 100 - 2Q and total cost TC = 50 + 10Q + 3Q². Find the profit-maximizing quantity, price and profit.
